steps.text: Divide goat cheese into 12 equal portions; roll each into a ball.
Combine pecans and cinnamon in a bowl. Roll cheese balls in pecan mixture until covered. Gently pat balls into patties; transfer to a serving plate.
Drizzle honey over patties; sprinkle rosemary on top. Serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Creamy Goat Cheese and Honey
raw_recipe.description: Creamy goat cheese is lightly dusted with pecans, honey, and rosemary. Spread it on your favorite crostini, bagel chips, or melba toasts as an appetizer.
raw_recipe.name: Creamy Goat Cheese and Honey

review.reviewBody:
I was struggling for some appetizer or dip idea for a party I was headed to, and stumbled upon this glorious little recipe. I followed the recipe instructions, but found myself having difficulty visualizing the little cheese balls just hanging out and being eaten at a bbq, so I basically dumped all of the cheese into the bowl and made one large cheese ball. IT WAS INCREDIBLE. I drizzled the rosemary honey on top (and reapplied throughout the evening as needed), and everybody was blown away. People were literally standing in awe in front of the bowl - that's how good it was.

As far as pecans go, I somehow found these Emerald Nuts Pecan Pie glazed pecans, and I think the extra sweetness pushed this recipe over the edge from yummy to go away this bowl is mine get your own. EVERYBODY loved it. I've committed this to memory and will definitely be making it again, probably even better around the holidays.

I didn't measure anything, used honey chevre from Trader Joe's, rolled in pecans I had crushed in the food processor with the cinnamon, drizzled with honey and crushed some dried rosemary in the palm of my hand before sprinkling on top. Really cute and yummy stuff. Thanks!

I made this into a spread just by softening the cheese and mixing everything together with the back of a spoon. Delish! The combination of flavors was great. Oh, I didn't have pecans on hand so I used almonds, and toasted them first -- they add a nice texture and nuttiness to the whole thing. Easy & yummy, 5 stars.
I deconstructed this recipe and made it into a salad by adding romaine, dried cherries and balsamic vinaigrette! I also subbed toasted almonds for pecans. It was awesome!

i liked this as an appetizer :) however, i also tried it as a meal. i boiled up some boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut them in half, put a few of these cheese balls (according to the recipe) inside the halves. then i stuck the chicken in a pan , whipped up some cream of mushroom soup, and when the cheese in the chicken was melted a bit, i served the chicken with some soup on top. My husband and i loved it! something about these appetizers made a perfect stuffing...and a quick meal too! only took about 45 minutes total to do everything, muti-tasking of course :)

I've been making this for several years now. I just buy the goat cheese "logs", open the package, drizzle honey and nuts on top, add a dash of nutmeg and serve with fruit and/or crackers. It's delish and presents beautifully.

very good, I had company and everybody was impressed. I had to change the nuts part, as I have an allergic person. But I used sesame seeds and it was a good solution. Everybody raved about the mixing of flavours and the delicate taste. Will repeat surely!

Super simple yet elegant appetizer. Be sure to bring the goat cheese to room temperature though. I added some crushed almonds to the goat cheese before drizzling the honey. You can also just throw everything into the food processor and use it as a bagel spread!

I loved this! Of course I love goat cheese in general. I kept the goat cheese in its log form and just rolled it in the other ingredients. Drizzled the honey on top and served with crackers. It presented well. Served at a family get together and it was a hit. Very easy appetizer!
I love goat cheese and this is a delicious and easy way to enjoy it. I made one large cheese ball versus 12 individual ones and served with Trader Joe's Golden Round Crackers. Perfection!
Don't roll into balls layer in a small casserol dish ommit the rosemary and use as an apple dip
Easy and delicious!!
A great add to a charcuterie board!
Made a spread instead w/ it. Delicious!!!
Everyone at a party I catered really loved them! If you or your guest like goat cheese they will like them
Great flavor! I used rosemary crackers to serve this on and it was a hit.
Cloyingly sweet, the combination of cinnamon and goat cheese was unpalatable.

Made this for a get together with friends. Everyone seemed to like it! I just made it according to the recipe but I did use candied pecans like one reviewer suggested and served it with those little toast crackers. It took a while to roll and coat the balls, but I think you get more flavor in each serving that way!

So simple to make this complex flavored bite! Didn't make any changes and loved it! It doesn't need a cracker, just pop 'me in your mouth and enjoy. I put three bites on top of a plain lettuce salad with raspberry vinegarette dressing and the salad became the best part of the meal! Will be making these more often!
Delicious recipe! I used chopped walnuts instead of pecans. Flavors work perfectly together & I'll definitely be making it again!
